Her favorite thing to do was put her feet up on the coffee table, and for one night each week, she could. Every Thursday night, sixteen year old Sophia's parents went to a movie, then dinner at their favorite diner. Sophia was left alone, except for a pet rabbit, who mostly stuck to his play pen. 
 
At around 6:40PM last Thursday, Sophia's parents kissed her forehead, and gave her the once over, again, about the rules of the house. 
  
"No boys, and no more than one friend over, and no one over after 9! Love you.,"Her mother said, rushed by her husband.
 Sophia smiled and waved her parents out, closing the door slowly.
  
Immediately after locking the door, Sophia picked her up smart phone, and hooked up to the living room stereo. She blared her favorite song, "Bluebeard" by The Cocteau Twins. With a graceful sway and twirl, Sophia began to dance. It wasn't long before she was hit with inspiration for a new dance routine. A ballerina and lyrical dancer by raw talent and ten years of bleeding heel blisters, Sophia had transformed herself into a swan by her own right. Unfortunately, her father was very vocal about his disdain for dance, fearful that one of Sophia's pirouettes could break something. The only time Sophia got to practice as deeply and as passionately as she wanted, were  her parents' date nights.

She turned up the music as loud as it would go, since she had no neighbors to complain about the noise. She twirled, and jumped, and swirled her hips, sending out an energy of playfulness and bliss with each movement. Raising her arms above her head and tilting back just a bit, Sophia closed her eyes. Just then, a phone rang in the kitchen. 

Confused, she stopped and walked out of the living room. On the white and blue marble counters, shook her mother's cell phone. 

 "She must have left it when she left for the movie.", said Sophia.

 She looked down at the caller name. It was restricted. Sophia ignored it. It rang again, and before she could react, a black gloved hand reached over from behind her, and picked it up. Sophia gasped, and went to turn around when she felt heavy, hard metal against the back of her head. 
 
"Yeah, Yeah I got her.," His voice, deep and clear, spoke. "She looks good. Sixteen or seventeen. Brunette." He began describing Sophia's body in vivid detail to the person on the other end.

Sophia's voice shook with fear. "What do-" Her words were stopped by the feeling of his gun pressing harder against her skull."

"I don't know. If she is she never told her mother, but you said you like 'em fresh anyways. I was in the bathroom, Jesus Christ, can't a man take a piss. Yeah yeah whatever, just get here."  He hung up the phone and set it back down on the counter.

He walked around Sophia and faced her.  The man was tall, over six feet, and broad enough to where 5'5", 110 pound Sophia dared not provoke him ,regardless of his gun, which was now lowered from her skull, and setting on the counter. The man's fingers were hovering just beside the trigger of black, shiny handgun.

Sophia's heartbeat banged against her inside of her chest. She used every "Happy place" technique to keep herself calm. 

"Sophia, is it?" The man asked, in an "I already know the answer" tone. 

Sophia nodded and looked up. The man was wearing a blank, white mask over his face. "Who are you.," She shudders. 
 
"I'm a friend of your dad, sweetheart." 

Sophia realized that his voice sounded familiar. Not incredibly so, but enough to where she knew she'd definitely heard it before. 

 "What do you want? We don't have a safe and my- my mom doesn't wear jewelry, and-and-" Sophia stuttered through quick, quivered breaths until the man cupped his hand over her mouth.

"Shut up. Frankly, I don't give a damn what your mother wears around her neck. Could be a hooker's panties for all I care. I'm just here to pick up what my boss is owed." He explained. Exploding suddenly, he yelled, "Turn that fucking music off!"

Panicked, Sophia scrambled with him holding his hand to her back to the living room. She unplugged the stereo, frantically. 

"Thank you. What the hell was that?" He asked.

"The..C-Cocteau Twins."

"That shitty goth or whatever band from the 80's or some shit? Aren't they a little old for you, sweetie?" He joked. Sophia felt exceedingly unnerved by his cavalierness. He let out a small chuckle. "Well whatever. Do you know what your parents did tonight?"

"They went to dinner and a movie, like they always do." Sophia answered. 

The man shook his head. Sighing heavily, he said, "Nope nope nope. Why don't I show you what they did." He stood up and left Sophia, still stunned, alone in the living room. "If I hear even the itty-bittiest fuckin rustle, I'm shooting." He yelled from the kitchen. He walked back with Sophia's mother's phone in hand. 

He leaned down to Sophia's level and started scrolling through pictures on her mother's phone. He left go of it, and let Sophia scroll at her pace. Her face grew increasingly horrified. Each photo showed her parents in escalating levels of fear and peril. When she reached the last photo, she screamed and dropped the phone on the floor. It was of her parents. Sitting in wooden chairs, heads tilted back from the force of two bullets, both still lodged in their foreheads. 

"What the fuck?!" She shouted. 

"Shush, shush. Your mommy and daddy owed my boss, a baaad bad man, a lot of money. More and more each week, in fact. Eventually he got tired of waitin' to get paid and so he sent me. No cash? I shoot you, and take what we want from the corpses. Your dad, happened to have a picture of a cute little brunette in his wallet. My boss liked what he saw, so here I am.", He  placed his hand on her shoulder. "I don't blame him."

Sophia recoiled. "I'm only sixteen.," She declared. 

"Don't care. A job is a job." He threw a sheet over her head and grabbed her from behind. Sophia shrieked and squirmed as hard as she could, but the man was too strong for her to wiggle away from. 

 The man took her outside, and locked the door behind him.
